architecture.mechanism: Ice adhesion strength on offshore wind turbine blade surfaces is governed predominantly by salt content, with ambient temperature and wind speed as secondary factors, and strong salt–wind and salt–temperature interactions; mastering these adhesive characteristics is the basis for effective ice removal.
architecture.intervention: Apply a salt-repellent (anti-fouling) coating to the blade airfoil surface that blocks salt crystal retention, thereby lowering ice adhesion strength so ice sheds under high wind loads, and schedule de-icing cycles preferentially toward the warmer end of the −3 °C~−15 °C operating window where adhesion is reduced.
architecture.expected_effect: Lower ice adhesion strength on coated blades allows passive or low-energy ice shedding in high winds, preserving aerodynamic performance and winter power output while the coating itself resists salt spray corrosion.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure ice adhesion strength on salt-repellent-coated versus uncoated NACA0018 airfoil coupons at −3 °C~−15 °C, 6 m/s~15 m/s wind, and 1~20 mg/m3 salt content; if adhesion on the coated coupons is not significantly lower than on uncoated coupons at high salt content, the mechanism is falsified.
